title: The input/output complexity of sorting and related problems
summary: Introduces the external-memory (I/O) model: computation cost is measured by block transfers between a small fast memory and a large slow one, and proves tight I/O bounds for sorting and permuting.

title: LambdaNetworks: Modeling long-range interactions without attention
summary: Replaces attention with ‘lambda layers’ that summarize context into linear functions, capturing long-range interactions at lower memory cost for vision models.

title: Longformer: The long-document transformer
summary: Combines sliding-window local attention with task-specific global tokens so attention scales linearly with sequence length, enabling documents of thousands of tokens.

title: An updated set of basic linear algebra subprograms (BLAS)
summary: The reference specification of the BLAS interface — the standard low-level kernels (vector, matrix-vector, matrix-matrix) whose blocked, memory-aware implementations underpin numerical computing.

title: Language models are few-shot learners
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
summary: GPT-3: a 175B-parameter autoregressive language model showing that scale alone yields strong few-shot, in-context learning across many NLP tasks.

title: Neural legal judgment prediction in English
venue: Proceedings of the 57th Annual Meeting of the ACL
summary: Releases the ECtHR dataset of European Court of Human Rights cases and benchmarks neural models on predicting violated articles from long case texts.

title: Paragraph-level rationale extraction through regularization: A case study on European Court of Human Rights cases
summary: Studies extracting paragraph-level rationales for legal judgment predictions on ECtHR, adding regularizers so the selected evidence is faithful and useful.

title: Kernel operations on the GPU, with autodiff, without memory overflows
summary: KeOps: a library that computes kernel and distance-matrix reductions on GPU without materializing the full matrix, using symbolic ‘lazy tensors’ with autodiff support.

title: Scatterbrain: Unifying sparse and low-rank attention
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS)
summary: Shows sparse and low-rank approximations capture complementary parts of attention and combines them (via LSH plus kernel features) for a more accurate, efficient approximation.

title: Training deep nets with sublinear memory cost
summary: Popularized gradient checkpointing for deep nets: store only a subset of activations and recompute the rest during backprop, trading compute for O(√n) memory.

title: Generating long sequences with sparse transformers
summary: Sparse Transformer: factorized strided/fixed attention patterns reduce attention cost to O(n√n), with block-sparse GPU kernels enabling very long sequences.

title: Rethinking attention with Performers
summary: Performer approximates softmax attention with positive orthogonal random features (FAVOR+), giving an unbiased, linear-time and linear-memory estimator.

title: Revisiting transformer-based models for long document classification
summary: Benchmarks Longformer-style and hierarchical Transformers on MIMIC-III and ECtHR, showing that processing longer inputs substantially helps long-document classification.

title: Transformer-XL: Attentive language models beyond a fixed-length context
venue: Proceedings of the 57th Annual Meeting of the ACL
summary: Adds segment-level recurrence and relative positional encodings so a Transformer can reuse hidden states from previous segments, extending effective context.

title: Learning fast algorithms for linear transforms using butterfly factorizations
summary: Parameterizes linear maps as products of butterfly matrices and shows they can learn fast algorithms such as the FFT and DCT directly from data.

title: Kaleidoscope: An efficient, learnable representation for all structured linear maps
summary: Kaleidoscope matrices — products of butterflies — can represent any structured linear map with near-optimal parameters and runtime, and serve as drop-in learnable layers.

title: Pixelated butterfly: Simple and efficient sparse training for neural network models
summary: Uses a fixed, hardware-friendly ‘flat block butterfly + low-rank’ sparsity pattern to train sparse MLPs and attention faster — the pattern later reused by block-sparse FlashAttention.

title: Monarch: Expressive structured matrices for efficient and accurate training
summary: Monarch matrices (products of block-diagonal matrices and permutations) are expressive yet GPU-efficient, speeding up training and fine-tuning of large models.

title: SMYRF: Efficient attention using asymmetric clustering
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
summary: Approximates attention by clustering queries and keys with asymmetric LSH into balanced groups, working as a drop-in replacement for pretrained models.

title: A two-pronged progress in structured dense matrix vector multiplication
venue: Proceedings of the 29th ACM-SIAM Symposium on Discrete Algorithms (SODA)
summary: Gives near-optimal algorithms for matrix-vector multiplication across a broad family of structured matrices defined by recurrences, unifying many known classes.

title: The working set model for program behavior
summary: Defines the ‘working set’ — the pages a program actively uses in a time window — as the basis for memory management and paging decisions.

title: BERT: Pre-training of deep bidirectional transformers for language understanding
summary: Pretrains a bidirectional Transformer encoder with masked-language-modeling and next-sentence objectives, setting new state of the art after fine-tuning on many NLP tasks.

title: Learning to prune deep neural networks via layer-wise optimal brain surgeon
summary: Extends Optimal Brain Surgeon to prune each layer independently using second-order information, with bounds on the resulting performance drop.

title: An image is worth 16x16 words: Transformers for image recognition at scale
summary: Vision Transformer (ViT): splits images into patches treated as tokens and shows a plain Transformer rivals CNNs when pretrained on large datasets.

title: On a new class of structured matrices
summary: Introduces quasi-separable matrices, whose off-diagonal blocks are low-rank, and gives fast algorithms for inversion and multiplication with them.

title: Fast geometric learning with symbolic matrices
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
summary: Applies KeOps symbolic matrices to geometric deep learning, computing large point-cloud and graph reductions on GPU with low memory.

title: Parameterized Complexity Theory
summary: Standard textbook on parameterized complexity: analysing problem hardness in terms of an extra parameter beyond input size (FPT, W-hierarchy).

title: The lottery ticket hypothesis: Finding sparse, trainable neural networks
summary: Dense networks contain sparse sub-networks (‘winning tickets’) that, trained from their original initialization, match the full network’s accuracy.

title: Stabilizing the lottery ticket hypothesis
summary: Shows winning tickets in larger networks can be found by rewinding weights to an early training iteration rather than to initialization.

title: Linear mode connectivity and the lottery ticket hypothesis
summary: Connects lottery tickets to linear mode connectivity: sparse sub-networks train to full accuracy only once they become stable to SGD noise.

title: It’s raw! Audio generation with state-space models
summary: SaShiMi: a multi-scale S4 state-space architecture for raw-waveform audio generation that trains stably and generates faster than autoregressive baselines.

title: OpenWebText corpus
summary: An open reproduction of OpenAI’s WebText corpus — web pages linked from highly-upvoted Reddit posts — widely used for GPT-2-style pretraining.

title: Data cube: A relational aggregation operator generalizing group-by, cross-tab, and sub-totals
summary: Introduces the CUBE operator and classifies aggregates as distributive, algebraic or holistic — the ‘algebraic aggregation’ idea behind FlashAttention’s block-wise softmax.

title: Evaluating derivatives: principles and techniques of algorithmic differentiation
summary: Comprehensive reference on automatic differentiation, including forward/reverse modes and checkpointing strategies that trade recomputation for memory.

title: HiPPO: Recurrent memory with optimal polynomial projections
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS)
summary: Frames online memory as projecting a signal’s history onto polynomial bases, yielding principled recurrent updates that underlie later state-space models.

title: Combining recurrent, convolutional, and continuous-time models with linear state space layers
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
summary: Linear State Space Layers (LSSL) unify RNNs, CNNs and continuous-time models, showing a state-space model can be viewed as all three.

title: Efficiently modeling long sequences with structured state spaces
summary: S4: a structured parameterization that makes state-space models efficient to compute, achieving strong results on Long Range Arena including Path-X.

title: Learning both weights and connections for efficient neural networks
summary: Magnitude pruning with retraining removes most connections from CNNs (e.g. 9–13×) without loss of accuracy.

title: Deep compression: Compressing deep neural networks with pruning, trained quantization and Huffman coding
summary: A three-stage pipeline — pruning, weight sharing/quantization and Huffman coding — that shrinks networks by 35–49× with no accuracy loss.

title: Memory hierarchy design
summary: The classic textbook chapter on caches and memory hierarchies — locality, bandwidth and latency trade-offs that motivate IO-aware algorithms.

title: The hardware lottery
summary: Argues research ideas often win because they suit available hardware and software rather than because they are universally better.

title: Transformer quality in linear time
summary: FLASH: a gated attention unit with chunked mixed local/linear attention that matches Transformer quality at linear cost.

title: Data movement is all you need: A case study on optimizing transformers
venue: Proceedings of Machine Learning and Systems
summary: Shows Transformer training is dominated by data movement rather than FLOPs and recovers large speedups via operator fusion and layout optimization.

title: Dissecting the Ampere GPU architecture via microbenchmarking
summary: Microbenchmarks of NVIDIA A100 memory hierarchy — latencies and bandwidths of registers, shared memory/L1, L2 and HBM.

title: Dissecting the NVIDIA Volta GPU architecture via microbenchmarking
summary: Detailed microbenchmark study of the V100 GPU revealing undocumented memory-hierarchy characteristics, instruction latencies and tensor-core behavior.

title: Dissecting the Graphcore IPU architecture via microbenchmarking
summary: Microbenchmarks Graphcore’s IPU, characterizing its large on-chip SRAM, interconnect bandwidth and compute throughput.

title: MIMIC-III, a freely accessible critical care database
summary: A large de-identified database of ICU patient records, including clinical notes and discharge summaries, widely used for medical NLP.

title: In-datacenter performance analysis of a tensor processing unit
venue: Proceedings of the 44th International Symposium on Computer Architecture (ISCA)
summary: Describes Google’s first TPU, a systolic-array inference accelerator, and shows it delivers far better performance per watt than contemporary CPUs and GPUs.

title: Displacement ranks of matrices and linear equations
venue: Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications
summary: Introduces displacement rank, a measure of how ‘Toeplitz-like’ a matrix is, enabling fast algorithms for structured linear systems.

title: Transformers are RNNs: Fast autoregressive transformers with linear attention
summary: Replaces softmax with a kernel feature map so attention becomes linear in sequence length and autoregressive decoding becomes an RNN.

title: Reformer: The efficient transformer
summary: Uses locality-sensitive hashing to attend only among similar keys (O(n log n)) plus reversible layers and chunking to cut memory.

title: ALBERT: A lite BERT for self-supervised learning of language representations
summary: Reduces BERT’s parameters via factorized embeddings and cross-layer sharing, and adds a sentence-order prediction loss.

title: The deep learning compiler: A comprehensive survey
venue: IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems
summary: Surveys DL compilers (TVM, XLA, Glow, …) — their IRs, frontends and backend optimizations such as operator fusion.

title: Sub-linear memory: How to make Performers slim
summary: Shows linear-attention Performers can be trained with memory sub-linear in sequence length via a chunked forward/backward computation.

title: Runtime neural pruning
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
summary: Learns, via reinforcement learning, to prune convolution channels adaptively per input at inference time.

title: RoBERTa: A robustly optimized BERT pretraining approach
summary: Revisits BERT pretraining — more data, longer training, larger batches, dynamic masking, no NSP — and substantially improves results.

title: Luna: Linear unified nested attention
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
summary: Approximates attention with two nested linear attentions through a fixed-length extra sequence, giving linear time and memory.

title: MLPerf training benchmark
venue: Proceedings of Machine Learning and Systems
summary: The MLPerf industry benchmark suite measuring time-to-train to a target quality across standard ML workloads, including BERT.

title: Scalability! But at what COST?
venue: 15th Workshop on Hot Topics in Operating Systems (HotOS XV)
summary: Shows many ‘scalable’ distributed graph systems are slower than a well-written single-threaded program, proposing the COST metric.

title: Online normalizer calculation for softmax
summary: Computes the softmax max and normalizer in a single pass by rescaling a running sum — the trick FlashAttention’s tiling builds on.

title: NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPU architecture
summary: NVIDIA’s whitepaper for the Volta V100 GPU, introducing Tensor Cores and HBM2 memory.

title: NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU architecture
summary: Whitepaper for the Ampere A100: third-generation Tensor Cores, 40–80 GB HBM2(e), larger on-chip SRAM and L2.

title: NVIDIA H100 Tensor Core GPU architecture
summary: Whitepaper for the Hopper H100 with FP8 Transformer Engine, HBM3 and thread-block clusters — compute continues to outpace memory bandwidth.

title: Random butterfly transformations with applications in computational linear algebra
summary: Uses randomized butterfly matrices to precondition linear systems so Gaussian elimination can avoid pivoting.

title: PyTorch: An imperative style, high-performance deep learning library
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
summary: Describes PyTorch’s define-by-run design, which keeps Python-first usability while achieving competitive performance.

title: Self-attention does not need O(n²) memory
summary: Shows exact attention can be computed with O(√n) or O(log n) memory by chunking and lazy softmax, using checkpointing for the backward pass.

title: Language models are unsupervised multitask learners
summary: GPT-2: a 1.5B-parameter language model trained on WebText that performs many tasks zero-shot.

title: Do transformers need deep long-range memory?
venue: Proceedings of the 58th Annual Meeting of the ACL
summary: Finds that only a few layers need long-range memory; limiting most layers to short local attention keeps language-modeling quality.

title: Compressive transformers for long-range sequence modelling
summary: Extends Transformer-XL memory with a compressed memory of older activations; introduces the PG-19 long-book benchmark.

title: Halide: A language and compiler for optimizing parallelism, locality, and recomputation in image processing pipelines
summary: Separates an image algorithm from its schedule (tiling, fusion, recomputation), letting programmers explore locality trade-offs without rewriting code.

title: Database management systems
summary: Standard database textbook covering I/O-efficient join algorithms, buffer management and external sorting.

title: Parallel stochastic gradient algorithms for large-scale matrix completion
summary: Jellyfish: a parallel SGD scheme that partitions the matrix so workers update disjoint blocks without locking.

title: Combiner: Full attention transformer with sparse computation cost
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
summary: Keeps full attention’s expressivity at sub-quadratic cost by factorizing attention as a structured conditional expectation over local and abstract regions.

title: Efficient content-based sparse attention with routing transformers
venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
summary: Routing Transformer clusters queries and keys with online k-means and attends within clusters, giving O(n^1.5) content-based sparse attention.

title: XLA: Compiling machine learning for peak performance
summary: Overview of XLA, the TensorFlow/JAX compiler that fuses operations and specializes kernels for CPUs, GPUs and TPUs.

title: Movement pruning: Adaptive sparsity by fine-tuning
summary: Prunes weights according to how they move during fine-tuning rather than their magnitude, excelling at high sparsity for pretrained models.

title: Megatron-LM: Training multi-billion parameter language models using model parallelism
summary: Intra-layer tensor model parallelism for Transformers, used to train 8.3B GPT-2 and 3.9B BERT models across hundreds of GPUs.

title: Structured transforms for small-footprint deep learning
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
summary: Uses Toeplitz-like, low-displacement-rank matrices as compact, fast layers for on-device speech models.

title: Adaptive attention span in transformers
venue: Proceedings of the Annual Meeting of the ACL
summary: Lets each attention head learn its own context span, so most heads stay short and a few reach very long contexts.

title: Long Range Arena: A benchmark for efficient transformers
summary: A benchmark of long-context tasks (ListOps, Text, Retrieval, Image, Pathfinder, Path-X) for comparing efficient Transformers on quality and speed.

title: Efficient transformers: A survey
summary: A taxonomy of efficient Transformer variants — fixed patterns, learned patterns, low-rank, kernels, recurrence and memory.

title: Attention is all you need
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
summary: Introduces the Transformer, built entirely from multi-head self-attention and feed-forward layers, replacing recurrence for sequence transduction.

title: DeepNet: Scaling transformers to 1,000 layers
summary: DeepNorm, a modified residual normalization with principled initialization, stabilizes training of Transformers up to 1,000 layers.

title: Linformer: Self-attention with linear complexity
summary: Observes the attention matrix is approximately low-rank and projects keys and values to a fixed length, giving linear-time attention.

title: Roofline: An insightful visual performance model for multicore architectures
summary: The Roofline model bounds attainable performance by peak compute and memory bandwidth × arithmetic intensity — the lens for compute- vs memory-bound kernels.

title: A data locality optimizing algorithm
venue: Proceedings of the ACM SIGPLAN 1991 Conference on PLDI
summary: A compiler algorithm that applies loop transformations and tiling to maximize data reuse in the cache.

title: Transformers: State-of-the-art natural language processing
summary: The Hugging Face Transformers library: a unified API and model hub for pretrained Transformer architectures.

title: Optimal space lower bounds for all frequency moments
summary: Proves tight space lower bounds for approximating frequency moments in the data-stream model.

title: Pay less attention with lightweight and dynamic convolutions
summary: Lightweight and dynamic convolutions, with kernels predicted per time step, match self-attention on translation and summarization at linear cost.

title: Nyströmformer: A Nyström-based algorithm for approximating self-attention
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
summary: Approximates softmax attention with the Nyström method using landmark queries and keys, giving linear complexity; includes careful LRA reproductions.

title: Tokens-to-token ViT: Training vision transformers from scratch on ImageNet
summary: T2T-ViT progressively aggregates neighboring tokens to model local structure, letting ViTs train well from scratch on ImageNet.

title: Big Bird: Transformers for longer sequences
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
summary: Combines random, windowed and global attention for linear-cost sparse attention, and proves it remains a universal approximator and Turing complete.

title: An attention free transformer
summary: AFT replaces dot-product attention with element-wise operations over keys, values and learned position biases, giving linear memory.

title: Long-short transformer: Efficient transformers for language and vision
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
summary: Transformer-LS aggregates short-range sliding-window attention with a dynamic low-rank projection for long-range attention.
